lines.title: Here's Semantic Router dot net in VS Code. Copilot's chat, its agent mode, and the command line tools in the terminal, all on one router on your machine.
lines.add: In the chat's model picker, open manage language models, and add a custom endpoint. Give it a name and any key, and pick chat completions. The router speaks the other two as well.
lines.models: VS Code opens a small JSON file for the models. Add the router's names: auto lets the router decide, and best always takes the most capable model. Mark them as tool capable, so agent mode can use them.
lines.pick: Now pick auto, and chat as usual. Inline completions still come from Copilot itself. The router handles chat and agent mode.
lines.ask: A quick question about this file goes to a small local model.
lines.agent: Switch to agent mode and ask for a change across the project. That's a bigger job, so it goes up a tier. And while the agent works, every tool result goes back to the model that asked for it.
lines.utility: VS Code's own small jobs, like naming the chat, go to the smallest model.
lines.terminal: And the command line tools? Open the terminal right here. Claude Code, Copilot C L I and Codex all point at the same router, each with a few lines of setup.
lines.live: The Live page shows them side by side: the chat, the agent and the terminal, each turn on the model that fits it.
lines.end: That's Semantic Router dot net in VS Code. It's open source and MIT licensed. Install it with one command, and keep using the tools you like.
